title: Resort Deposit Nights by Season and Length of Stay — Room Reservations
content:
**Resort deposit schedule.** When the deposit a Room Reservations resort reservation requires is worked out again after a change raises its nightly rate, the number of nights the deposit covers follows the award season of the arrival night and the length of the stay. When the arrival night is in the peak season and the stay is at least 6 nights, the deposit covers 2 nights instead of the plan's resort deposit nights; when the arrival night is in the off-peak season and the stay is shorter than 3 nights, it covers 0 nights; any other stay keeps the plan's resort deposit nights.

The award season is the one recorded on the reservation for the arrival night; the stay is the nights from the arrival date to the departure date.

| Award season of the arrival night | Stay | Nights the deposit covers |
|---|---|---|
| Peak | 6 nights or more | 2 |
| Peak | 5 nights or fewer | the plan's resort deposit nights |
| Standard | any | the plan's resort deposit nights |
| Off-peak | 2 nights or fewer | 0 |
| Off-peak | 3 nights or more | the plan's resort deposit nights |

**Boundaries.** A peak-season stay of exactly 6 nights covers 2 nights; one of 5 nights does not. An off-peak stay of exactly 3 nights is not shorter than 3 nights, so it keeps the plan's resort deposit nights; one of 2 nights covers 0.

**Illustration (hypothetical nightly rate of 300.00, tax 10%).** A peak-season stay of 7 nights: the deposit by nights is 2 nights multiplied by 300.00, multiplied by 1.10, that is 660.00. An off-peak stay of 2 nights: 0 nights, so 0.00.
